# Sluice v1 decisions

## Implementation decisions

| ID | Date | Area or IDs | Decision | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DI-1 | 2026-09-10 | Ledger | A named slice ID without prefix (for example `EXR-004`) maps to `REQ-<id>` when that requirement exists, otherwise to `SCN-<id>`. `SEC-012` maps to `SCN-SEC-012`. | No `REQ-SEC-012` exists in the SDD. |
| DI-2 | 2026-09-10 | REQ-CORE-003, D-10 | Migrations use goose file format (`-- +goose Up`) but a small embedded runner applies them. All pending migrations run in one transaction after `pg_advisory_xact_lock`. Versions are in `schema_migrations`. | goose v3.28 lockers are session-scoped or table-based. REQ-CORE-003 requires a transaction-scoped advisory lock. sqlc still reads the goose files. |
| DI-3 | 2026-09-10 | REQ-CORE-006 | Lease expiry and leader guards use the application clock value as a statement parameter, not `now()`. | Fake-clock scenarios (SCN-TRG-004, SCN-STO-005) need control of time. Instances use NTP-synced clocks. |
| DI-4 | 2026-09-10 | §5 | Migration `00001_init.sql` holds the full §5 data model plus helper columns (for example `task_runs.cancel_requested`, `not_before`, `executions.deadline_at`). It is edited in place until v1 release. | No deployment exists before v1. One schema file is simpler to review. |
| DI-5 | 2026-09-10 | C-06 | The pgx pool uses `QueryExecModeExec` with statement and description caches off. Migrations run in simple protocol. | Unnamed statements work through PgBouncer transaction mode. |
| DI-6 | 2026-09-10 | D-09, REQ-API-002 | Request validation uses kin-openapi `openapi3filter` against the embedded spec. Failures return 422 `validation_failed` with `{field, message}` details. | One contract source. Field details come from the schema errors. Superseded in slice R (D-09, D-10, D-22, D-23). |
| DI-7 | 2026-09-10 | D-10 | sqlc generates static queries into `internal/platform/dbq`. Queries with dynamic filters use hand-written pgx SQL. | sqlc cannot express optional filters without complex SQL. Superseded in slice R (D-09, D-10, D-22, D-23). |
| DI-8 | 2026-09-10 | §10.2 | Superseded in slice R (D-09, D-10, D-22, D-23): `buildtool` keeps only forbid, trace, size-check and setup, and huma generates `api/openapi.yaml`. History: `buildtool` (Go, `tools/buildtool`) implemented forbid, trace, ledger-check, verify, evidence, evidence-check, size-check and setup. Ledger evidence format was `path::TestName`. Go tools sqlc, oapi-codegen and gotestsum were pinned with the `tool` directive in `go.mod`. | One language for the tooling. Pinned generators keep `gen-check` stable. |
| DI-9 | 2026-09-10 | Test layers | Superseded in slice R: `just test` runs unit and integration tests together, and `tests/review/` no longer exists (SDD §10.2, §4.4). History: Go tests used build tags: none for unit, `integration` for testcontainers tests ([I] and `tests/review`), `e2e` for `tests/e2e`, `k8s` for `tests/k8s`, `perf` for `tests/perf`. Playwright tests live in `tests/ui`. | `just test` and `just test-int` had to select different sets. |
| DI-10 | 2026-09-10 | REQ-UI-010 | Fonts are self-hosted with `@fontsource` packages. | The CSP `default-src 'self'` (SI-12) blocks font CDNs. |
| DI-11 | 2026-09-10 | REQ-AUTH-006, SI-03 | Permissions live in `internal/auth/permissions.go`: one entry per operationId and per non-OpenAPI router pattern. The validator middleware authorizes before request validation. Operation IDs are normalized to lower camel case because the spec embedded by oapi-codegen capitalizes them. | One table for the route inventory test. A caller without permission never sees validation details. Superseded in slice R: see D-23. Each operation declares its access with `httpx.Op`, and the permission table is gone. |
| DI-12 | 2026-09-10 | SI-06 | Cookie-authenticated unsafe requests need an `Origin` equal to the public origin or the request host, or `Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin`. A request with neither header is rejected with 403 `csrf_failed`. | Secure default. Browsers send one of the headers. |
| DI-13 | 2026-09-10 | REQ-AUTH-003, REQ-AUTH-004 | New passwords need at least 10 characters. Admin-created users and admin resets set a temporary password. `sluice user create` and `reset-password` set a final password unless `--temporary` is given. | NIST 800-63B minimum is 8. The CLI is the recovery path. |
| DI-14 | 2026-09-10 | Appendix B | `GET /api/v1/instances` needs admin, because instances are a settings page. Token effective role is the lower of the token role and the current owner role. | Appendix B lists settings as admin. A demoted owner must not keep a higher token. |
| DI-15 | 2026-09-10 | REQ-AUTH-008 | Login failures are counted in `login_attempts` over a 15-minute window. `Retry-After` is the time until the oldest failure in the window leaves it. Rejected (429) attempts are not recorded. | Works across instances through Postgres. |
| DI-16 | 2026-09-10 | REQ-UI-010, SI-12 | The UI uses native `<dialog>` and `<select>` elements instead of Radix Dialog. | Radix Dialog injects `<style>` elements, which `default-src 'self'` blocks. |
| DI-17 | 2026-09-10 | REQ-STO-006 | Storage GC runs from the maintenance leader at most once in 24 hours (last run in `settings`). It deletes bundles unused for 7 days, file objects without a snapshot reference (row locked with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`), stored files without a row, and logs and artifacts whose execution row is gone. Objects younger than 1 hour are kept. | Saves take `FOR SHARE` on the file object row, so GC cannot delete content that a concurrent save references. The grace period protects uploads in progress. |
| DI-18 | 2026-09-10 | REQ-EXE-001, §6.4 | An execution stores its effective definition (flow model plus the `namespace.yaml` defaults of the pinned snapshot) in `executions.definition`. File runs store a synthetic flow with one `script` task. The instance default executor is `process`. | The definition and the snapshot cannot change after creation. `process` is always enabled (REQ-EXR-002). |
| DI-19 | 2026-09-10 | REQ-EXE-010, REQ-EXE-011 | Every instance runs the dispatcher (claims with `SKIP LOCKED`), starts queued executions and queues ready tasks. Each instance checks the heartbeat of its own claimed task runs through its executor. The maintenance leader also marks task runs of offline instances as `lost` and enforces flow deadlines. | Work is spread over instances without a broker (D-02). Only the claiming instance can check a local process. |
| DI-20 | 2026-09-10 | REQ-RUN-004, REQ-EXE-006 | The runner enforces the task timeout and cancel (SIGTERM, SIGKILL after 10 s). The claiming instance also polls `cancel_requested` every second for its process tasks, so a cancel does not wait for the 10 s heartbeat. The engine marks a running task `TIMED_OUT` when it passes its timeout by 60 s without completion. | Same behavior on all executors, with a server-side safety net. |
| DI-21 | 2026-09-10 | §6.6 | Dependencies that are `SKIPPED` with `run_if_not_met` do not satisfy `run_if: success`; the dependent is `SKIPPED` with `run_if_not_met`. A dependency that failed, timed out, was cancelled or was skipped with `upstream_failed` makes a `success` dependent `SKIPPED` with `upstream_failed`. | §6.6 defines success as all dependencies SUCCESS. The reason keeps the execution result rule of §6.6 correct. |
| DI-22 | 2026-09-10 | SDD §0 rule 1 | The SDD edit for slice R is a one-time exception to §0 rule 1. The human approved it in the design review (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-10-architecture-refactor-design.md`). Rule 1 stays in force after this. | The SDD is the only memory that survives a context refresh. It must describe the target architecture. |
| DI-23 | 2026-09-10 | D-09, SI-03 | Streamed operations (`getFile`, `uploadFile`, `streamExecutionLogs`, `downloadExecutionLogs`, `streamExecutionEvents`, `downloadArtifact`, `runnerGetBundle`, `runnerPutArtifact`) use `httpx.Raw`: a spec entry plus a plain chi handler behind the same access check. | These bodies must not be buffered. One access check for all routes. |
| DI-25 | 2026-09-11 | Build process, SDD §12, §13 | The session prompt names `docs/build/ledger.md`, `just verify`, `just evidence-check`, review rounds and SDD §14. SDD 1.1 has none of these, because slice R item R-13 removed them with human approval (DI-22). The build follows SDD 1.1: `handover.md` holds the state per slice, `just trace` gives the evidence, and SDD §13 defines done. | The SDD is authoritative (§0 rule 1). A new ledger would bring back a process that the human removed. |
| DI-26 | 2026-09-11 | REQ-TRG-002 | Schedule times are wall times in the trigger time zone. A wall time in a DST gap fires at the same wall time with the offset before the change, that is one gap later (02:30 on the Zurich spring day fires at 03:30 CEST). A wall time that exists twice fires once, at the first instant. | "Fires once per day" (SCN-TRG-002) needs a fire time on the spring day. The rule is the one of Vixie cron. |
| DI-27 | 2026-09-11 | REQ-TRG-002, REQ-TRG-003 | The scheduler leader ticks each second. A due time counts as missed when a later fire time also passed, or when it passed more than 30 s ago. `last` fires the latest passed time. `none` fires no missed time. Each tick advances `next_fire_at` with a compare-and-set update that checks the scheduler lease in the same statement. The execution insert and the pre-check on `(trigger_id, scheduled_for)` are in the same transaction. | Exactly-once across leader changes (D-14) without leader memory state. The 30 s grace covers normal tick delay. |
| DI-28 | 2026-09-11 | REQ-TRG-004, SI-05 | A webhook trigger has no key until an editor rotates it. `POST /api/v1/flows/{ns}/{flow}/triggers/{trigger}/webhook-key` returns the key and URL once. The trigger payload holds `body` (parsed when JSON, else text) and `headers` (lower-case names, first value). `Authorization`, `Cookie` and `Proxy-Authorization` are not stored. A disabled flow returns 409 `flow_disabled`, an invalid flow 422 `flow_invalid`, a removed trigger 404. | Keys are shown only once, so the server cannot create one in advance. Caller credentials must not become visible to viewers in the trigger payload. |
| DI-29 | 2026-09-11 | REQ-TRG-005 | A flow trigger without `states` fires on every end state. Flow triggers fire in the transaction that ends the upstream execution, each in a savepoint: a downstream start error (for example a bad input) writes a `trigger.failed` audit event and does not fail the upstream end. A chain depth above 10 writes `trigger.chain_depth_exceeded`. | §6.5 makes `states` optional. The upstream result must not depend on a downstream flow. |
| DI-30 | 2026-09-11 | REQ-SEC-001, Appendix B | Editors can list secret providers (name, type, configuration without credentials), so that the secret form can offer them. Provider create, update, delete and check need admin. Global secrets and variables have their own operations with admin access; namespace secrets and variables have operations with editor access. | Each operation declares one role (D-23). Editors must choose a provider for namespace secrets. |
| DI-31 | 2026-09-11 | REQ-SEC-002, REQ-SEC-007 | Secret and variable keys match `^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,127}$`. A namespace scope needs an existing namespace row (404 `namespace_not_found` otherwise); implicit parents get a row only when a user creates them. Builtin associated data is `<scope>/<key>` with scope `global` or the namespace name. A provider failure of a defined key fails the task with `secret_provider_error`, or `secret_not_found` when the provider has no value. | Keys must work in `secret('KEY')` and `vars.KEY`. Secrets reference namespaces by ID. |
| DI-32 | 2026-09-11 | SI-12, REQ-UI-007, SCN-UI-010 | CodeMirror styles go into one constructed style sheet per root (`adoptedStyleSheets`): `ui/src/components/editor/csp-styles.ts` replaces `StyleModule.mount` of style-mod and keeps its module order. Vite does not inline assets (`assetsInlineLimit: 0`). | The CSP `default-src 'self'` of SI-12 blocks the `<style>` elements of style-mod and `data:` fonts. Before this, the editor had no base styles and lint markers had no size. SI-12 fixes the header text, so a nonce is not possible. |
| DI-33 | 2026-09-11 | REQ-GIT-001 to REQ-GIT-005, SI-08 | Git uses go-git. Sync clones the branch head bare and shallow into a temporary directory and reads the tree from the object store, with no checkout; symlinks, submodules and invalid paths are skipped with a warning in the sync run. Push builds the new commit in memory from the last synced commit and pushes only the new branch. Repository URLs are `https://`, `ssh://` or `user@host:path`; plain `http://` is allowed only for loopback hosts. An ssh source without `known_hosts` does not check the host key and each run records a warning. A token goes as basic auth with user `x-access-token`. A source without a webhook secret refuses webhook calls. The runs of a source are not deleted. | No repository content reaches a file system, so crafted trees cannot write outside the directory. The local git fixture (§10.4) serves plain http on loopback. `known_hosts` is optional in REQ-GIT-001. |
| DI-34 | 2026-09-11 | REQ-EXR-002, REQ-EXR-004, REQ-EXR-009, REQ-DEP-001, REQ-DEP-005 | The docker executor uses the moby Engine API client from `DOCKER_HOST`. Task containers have no volumes or binds, run with `init`, and get `host.docker.internal:host-gateway` so that Linux engines reach the server. The runner binary is copied once from `SLUICE_RUNNER_IMAGE` into a cached tar file and from there into each created container at `/sluice-bin/sluice`. The entrypoint is `sluice exec` (from the image PATH when `inject_runner: false`). Cancel stops with a 10 s grace and removes the container. At start the executor removes stopped Sluice containers that an earlier server left. With `SLUICE_EXECUTORS=auto`, docker is on when the Docker API answers a ping within 2 s. `sluice-uv` is Debian slim with bash, uv, a uv-managed Python 3.12 and bun, user 65532. The compose file runs `sluice-uv` with the process executor, and its host port comes from `SLUICE_PORT`. | One client for all Engine calls. No bind mount of the runner (D-04, C-03). A server restart must not leave containers behind. |
| DI-35 | 2026-09-11 | REQ-EXR-002, REQ-EXR-005, REQ-EXR-006, REQ-DEP-002 | The kubernetes executor creates one Job per attempt with an init container `sluice runner-install /sluice-bin` and two `emptyDir` volumes (runner, workdir). The run token is in the Job environment: it is scoped to one task run and expires (SI-04); user secret values are never in the Job. With `auto`, kubernetes is on when a Job create dry run succeeds; without `SLUICE_K8S_NAMESPACE` or a service account namespace the Job namespace is `default`. The `k8s-reconcile:<pool>` leader passes every 60 s. Wait also ends early with `image_pull_failed`. A runner that reports `cancelled` without a requested cancel (for example a Job deleted by hand) ends the attempt FAILED with `lost`, so the retry policy applies. The chart runs the server as UID 65532 with a read-only root file system, an `emptyDir` at `/tmp` and a pod grace 10 s longer than `SLUICE_SHUTDOWN_GRACE`. `tests/k8s/run.sh` deploys Postgres and a Vault dev server with Kubernetes auth into the kind cluster as test substitutes. | One retry model on all executors (D-20). A hand-deleted Job is lost work, not a user cancel. |
| DI-36 | 2026-09-11 | REQ-EXE-001, REQ-TRG-004, NFR-002 | API triggers and webhooks load the flow and resolve the inputs before the create transaction starts. Only the scheduler and flow triggers create in a transaction of the caller, because their trigger state must change with the execution. The webhook `last_fired_at` update runs after the create; a failure of that update gives a warning log and does not fail the call. | A flow load inside the transaction needs a second pool connection. 55 concurrent triggers held all 10 connections and waited for each other until the request context ended (found with SCN-UI-004). |
| DI-37 | 2026-09-11 | REQ-UI-003 | The dashboard success rate is SUCCESS divided by the sum of SUCCESS, FAILED and TIMED_OUT in the range. CANCELLED and SKIPPED executions are not in the rate. Without such executions the rate is empty and the UI shows "—". | The SDD names the KPI but does not define it. A user or a condition causes a cancel or a skip, so these are not a result of the run. |
| DI-24 | 2026-09-10 | Slice R design, REQ-UI-* | Two deviations from the slice R design: the SSE client code lives in the executions feature components (`log-viewer` and `ExecutionPage`), not in `features/executions/api/`. `run-dialogs.tsx` and `execution-bits.tsx` stay in `components/`. | The SSE code serves only these components. The flows and executions features share the two component files. |
